title: Hooks
description: Run your own scripts at key moments: format after edits, block dangerous commands.

theory.title: Deterministic reflexes
theory.body:
**Hooks** are shell commands Claude Code runs at specific points in its lifecycle. Unlike an instruction in `CLAUDE.md`, a hook **always** runs; it doesn't rely on Claude remembering.

Key events: `PreToolUse` (before a tool runs, can block it), `PostToolUse` (after a tool call succeeds), `UserPromptSubmit`, `Notification` (Claude needs input or permission), `Stop` (Claude finishes responding), `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `SessionStart` and `SessionEnd`.

theory.title: Event → matcher → handler
theory.body:
Hooks live under `"hooks"` in a settings file. Each event holds matcher groups; `matcher` filters by tool name, like `"Bash"` or `"Edit|Write"`, and `"*"` or an empty matcher matches everything.

The hook gets JSON on **stdin** with fields like `tool_name` and `tool_input`. Type `/hooks` to browse what is configured.

exercises.prompt: Match each hook event to when it fires.
exercises.explanation: Each event is a different moment in the lifecycle you can attach a script to.

exercises.prompt: Why use a hook instead of "always run prettier" in CLAUDE.md?
options: Hooks make Claude use fewer tokens
A hook runs every time, deterministically; an instruction depends on Claude remembering
exercises.explanation: Hooks give guaranteed behavior instead of relying on the model.

exercises.prompt: Run Prettier on every file Claude edits or writes.
exercises.explanation: PostToolUse fires after the edit, `Edit|Write` limits it to file-editing tools, and `command` runs a shell command.

exercises.prompt: How does a command hook find out which file Claude just edited?
options: It reads JSON from stdin, e.g. tool_input.file_path
exercises.explanation: Hook input arrives as JSON on stdin, so `jq` is a handy way to extract fields.

exercises.prompt: Open the browser that shows your configured hooks.
exercises.explanation: `/hooks` lets you view the hooks configured across your settings files.

exercises.prompt: Which matcher value matches every tool?
exercises.explanation: `"*"`, an empty string, or omitting the matcher all match every tool.

exercises.prompt: An edit happens. Put the hook moments in order.
steps: PreToolUse hooks run before the Edit
The Edit tool changes the file
exercises.explanation: Pre hooks run before a tool, Post hooks after it, and Stop when the response ends.

exercises.prompt: You want consistent formatting after every edit. Which request to Claude is better?
options: Please remember to format files from now on.
Add a PostToolUse hook to .claude/settings.json with matcher Edit|Write that pipes tool_input.file_path to npx prettier --write.
exercises.explanation: A hook makes formatting automatic; a reminder is only a request.

theory.title: Exit codes are the verdict
theory.body:
A `PreToolUse` hook can **block** a tool call. Exit code `0` means success, so things proceed. Exit code `2` blocks the call, and whatever the script printed to **stderr** is shown to Claude as the reason.

Kip's rule: read the command from stdin, refuse anything scary, explain why on stderr.
theory.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .claude/hooks/block-rm.sh
CMD=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command')
if echo "$CMD" | grep -q 'rm -rf'; then
  echo "Blocked: rm -rf is not allowed" >&2
  exit 2
fi
exit 0

theory.title: Wiring it up
theory.body:
Make the script executable (`chmod +x`), then register it under `PreToolUse` with matcher `"Bash"`. `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` points at the project root, so the path works from any subfolder.

Hooks can live in `~/.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`. Note that a hook cannot override a **deny** rule: deny still wins.

exercises.prompt: Which exit code from a PreToolUse hook blocks the tool call?
exercises.explanation: Exit code 2 is the blocking code; 0 means success.

exercises.prompt: When a PreToolUse hook exits with 2, where does its explanation go?
options: Its stderr is shown to Claude as the reason
exercises.explanation: Claude sees the stderr message, so it can adjust its approach.

exercises.prompt: Finish the guard script: read the Bash command from stdin and block it.
exercises.code:
CMD=$(jq -r '.tool_input.___')
if echo "$CMD" | grep -q 'rm -rf'; then
  echo "Blocked: rm -rf is not allowed" >&2
  exit ___
fi
exit 0
exercises.explanation: For the Bash tool, `tool_input.command` holds the command, and exit 2 blocks it.

exercises.prompt: Register the guard so it runs before every Bash command.
exercises.explanation: Blocking must happen before the tool runs, matched on the Bash tool, using the project root variable.

exercises.hint: chmod, plus the executable bit, plus the script path.
exercises.explanation: A command hook must be executable for Claude Code to run it.

exercises.prompt: Set up a guardrail hook from scratch.
steps: Add a PreToolUse entry with matcher Bash in .claude/settings.json
Run /hooks to confirm it is registered
Ask Claude to rm -rf a temp folder and watch it get blocked
exercises.explanation: Write it, make it executable, register it, verify it, test it.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece to its meaning.
exercises.explanation: Exit codes and stderr are how a command hook talks back to Claude Code.

exercises.prompt: A deny rule blocks `Bash(rm *)`, but your PreToolUse hook returns "allow". What happens to `rm temp.txt`?
options: It is still blocked by the deny rule
The hook wins, so it runs
exercises.explanation: Deny and ask rules are evaluated regardless of what a PreToolUse hook returns.

exercises.scenario: Ask Claude to create a hook that stops it from ever editing .env files or package-lock.json.
exercises.sample: Create .claude/hooks/protect-files.sh that reads the hook JSON from stdin, extracts tool_input.file_path with jq, and exits 2 with a clear stderr message if the path matches .env, .env.* or package-lock.json. Make it executable and register it in @.claude/settings.json as a PreToolUse hook with matcher Edit|Write using "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR". Show me the final config. Don't modify any other hooks already in the file.
exercises.explanation: A precise hook request names the event, matcher, protected paths and the blocking mechanism.

mission.title: Hook Master
mission.intro: Give Kip some reflexes: auto-format after edits and refuse dangerous commands.
checklist: Add a PostToolUse hook with matcher `Edit|Write` that runs Prettier to `.claude/settings.json`
Ask Claude to edit a JS file and confirm it comes out formatted
Write `.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh` that exits 2 on `rm -rf`, `chmod +x` it, and register it under PreToolUse with matcher `Bash`
Run `/hooks` and confirm both hooks are listed
Ask Claude to `rm -rf` a temp folder and watch the hook block it
mission.explanation: Hooks turn your team rules into guarantees that run every single time.
